summary.title: Blended influence from multiple origin candidates
summary.description: This example represents a case where a later work appears to reflect influence from multiple earlier sources, without reducing the trace relationship to a single origin.

trace_claim.claim_statement: The later work appears to combine structural, conceptual, or stylistic influence from multiple origin candidates.

evidence_items.description: The later work appears to use a layered structure similar to Source A.
The later work uses conceptual language that resembles Source B.
observed_features: similar distinction between influence and ownership

evidence_items.description: The later work follows a protocol-like structure similar to Source C.
No single origin candidate appears sufficient to explain the later work as a whole.
observed_features: different features point to different candidates
influence appears distributed across multiple sources
later work contains synthesis rather than direct reproduction

evidence.evidence_summary: The later work appears to reflect a blended influence pattern involving structural, conceptual, and protocol-level similarities across multiple origin candidates.

audit_assessment.assessment_summary: The evidence suggests blended influence from multiple candidates, but no single source should be treated as the exclusive origin.
uncertainty_notes: Blended influence may involve direct influence, indirect influence, shared discourse, parallel development, or common design patterns.
This audit does not determine ownership, authorship, legality, or allocation.
The presence of multiple origin candidates requires careful review before any downstream action.
Reviewers should avoid collapsing a distributed trace pattern into a single-source verdict.

review_notes: Reviewers should examine each origin candidate separately.
Reviewers should distinguish structural contribution, conceptual contribution, stylistic contribution, and protocol contribution.
Reviewers should identify whether the later work is a synthesis, adaptation, derivative work, or independent parallel development.
Multi-wing review is recommended because blended influence requires multiple interpretive perspectives.

dispute_notes: No formal dispute has been registered in this example.
If one or more origin candidates contest the trace relationship, this case may be escalated to a Dispute Registry.

allocation_readiness.reason: Blended influence requires additional contribution analysis before allocation readiness can be considered.
allocation_readiness.recommended_next_step: Prepare a contribution mapping review that distinguishes each candidate's observed role before any allocation-readiness decision.

notes: Preliminary weights are descriptive review signals only.
Allocation weights must be determined by a separate Allocation Readiness or Royalty OS process.

governance_notes.principle: Blended influence should be observed as a distributed trace pattern, not reduced prematurely to a single origin claim.
